texts.facts: This application under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been filed for quashment of FIR registered in Crime No. 525/2022 at Police Station Barela, District Jabalpur for offence under Sections 498-A, 323, 506, 34 of IPC and under Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act registered against the applicant and other co-accused persons. 2. The applicant is the mother-in-law of respondent No. 2. Respondent No. 2 has lodged an FIR on the ground that on 03.05.2022, her marriage was performed with Pritesh Pandey, as per Hindu Rights and Rituals. Sufficient dowry was given by her parents as per their financial abilities. In spite of the fact that approximately Rs.15,00,000/- were spent by her father apart from giving the cash amount, household articles etc, the applicant and other co-accused persons used to beat her for demand of Rs.30,00,000/- and they were also threatening that her husband would perform second marriage. The respondent has been turned out of her matrimonial house and they are insisting that unless and until, the demand of dowry is fulfilled, she will not be allowed to enter inside her matrimonial house. 3. Challenging the FIR lodged by respondent No. 2, it is submitted that the co-accused had already expressed his apprehension that they may be falsely implicated. The allegations made in the FIR are false. It is further submitted that the respondent had stayed with her husband only for 10 to 12 days and from thereafter she is creating all sorts of trouble and she does not wish to reside with him. Thus, it is submitted that the FIR lodged against the applicant be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 4.
texts.arguments: It has been rightly submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that ordinarily power under Section 482 CrPC should not be used to quash an FIR because that amounts to interfering with the statutory power of the police to investigate a cognizable offence in accordance with the provisions of CrPC.

Section 482 is a sort of reminder to the High Courts that they are not merely courts of law, but also courts of justice and possess inherent powers to remove injustice.

Such powers can be exercised to secure ends of justice, prevent abuse of the process of any court and to make such orders as may be necessary to give effect to any order under this Code, depending upon the facts of a given case.
The Court can always take note of any miscarriage of justice and prevent the same by exercising its powers under Section 482 of the Code.
